# Accessor

<!-- gen:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:op-docs` from noodles-validate/registry.json. The title and the text between gen:begin and gen:end markers are replaced on every run; write anywhere else. -->

A function called for each row of your data and passed to Deck.gl layer properties. The current row is passed as the `d` variable (e.g., `d.population`, `d.properties.color`). Available variables: `d` (current row), `i` (index), `data` (all rows), `op()` (access operators), `sequenceTime` (timeline position), `frame` (current frame), `totalFrames`, `sequence` (timeline metadata). Includes d3, turf, and other utilities.
<!-- gen:end summary -->

## Syntax

<!-- gen:begin syntax -->
```json
{
  "id": "/accessor",
  "type": "AccessorOp",
  "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
  "data": { "inputs": {} }
}
```

Expressions and code read its fields as `op('/accessor').par.expression` (an input) and `op('/accessor').out.accessor` (an output). Edges name the same fields as handles: `par.expression`, `out.accessor`.
<!-- gen:end syntax -->

## Inputs

<!-- gen:begin inputs -->
| Name | Type | Default |
|------|------|---------|
| `expression` | `ExpressionField` | `""` |
<!-- gen:end inputs -->

## Outputs

<!-- gen:begin outputs -->
| Name | Type |
|------|------|
| `accessor` | `FunctionField` |
<!-- gen:end outputs -->

## Remarks

An Accessor doesn't compute a value. It builds a function, and the layer you connect it to calls that function once for each row of its data, with the row as `d`, its index as `i` and the layer's whole data as `data`. Connect `out.accessor` to a layer input whose name starts with `get`, such as `getPosition` or `getFillColor`, in place of a constant.

The expression becomes the body of `return <expression>`, so it has to be a single expression. Statements such as `const x = ...` or `if (...)` fail with a syntax error, which shows on the node. Put multi-step logic upstream in a [Code](./code.md) or [DuckDB](./duck-db.md) operator and let the accessor read the result.

An error thrown while evaluating one row is caught. The accessor returns `undefined` for that row and the node shows no error, so a row whose `d.properties` is missing quietly gets no value from `d.properties.name`. If some points are missing, check the rows rather than the node.

If the word `await` appears anywhere in the expression, even inside a string such as `d.status === 'await'`, the function is compiled as `async` and returns a Promise for every row. deck.gl can't use a Promise as a position or a color. Fetch data upstream instead.

Every Accessor runs again when the timeline playhead moves, whether or not the expression reads `sequenceTime` or `frame`. Each run hands the layer a new function, and layer operators list accessor inputs in the layer's `updateTriggers`, so deck.gl re-evaluates that attribute for every row. During playback that is every row on every frame. Keep the expression to reading and lightly reshaping fields of `d`, and do heavy work such as distance calculations or string parsing upstream, once.

Operators whose number or color inputs take accessors, such as [MapRange](./map-range.md), [Math](./math.md) and [ColorRamp](./color-ramp.md), accept an Accessor's output and return a per-row function in turn. That lets you scale or color by a column without writing the arithmetic into the expression.

## Examples

Place earthquakes from a CSV and size them by magnitude. The position accessor goes straight into the layer. The magnitude accessor goes through MapRange, whose output is also a per-row function. The [California Earthquakes](https://noodles.gl/app/examples/california-earthquakes) example is built the same way.

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "/quakes", "type": "FileOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "format": "csv", "url": "@/data.csv" } } },
    { "id": "/position", "type": "AccessorOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 150 }, "data": { "inputs": { "expression": "[d.Longitude, d.Latitude]" } } },
    { "id": "/magnitude", "type": "AccessorOp", "position": { "x": 0, "y": 300 }, "data": { "inputs": { "expression": "d.Magnitude" } } },
    { "id": "/radius", "type": "MapRangeOp", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 300 }, "data": { "inputs": { "inMin": 2.5, "inMax": 7, "outMin": 1000, "outMax": 20000 } } },
    { "id": "/points", "type": "ScatterplotLayerOp", "position": { "x": 600, "y": 0 }, "data": { "inputs": { "radiusUnits": "meters" } } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "id": "/quakes.out.data->/points.par.data", "source": "/quakes", "sourceHandle": "out.data", "target": "/points", "targetHandle": "par.data" },
    { "id": "/position.out.accessor->/points.par.getPosition", "source": "/position", "sourceHandle": "out.accessor", "target": "/points", "targetHandle": "par.getPosition" },
    { "id": "/magnitude.out.accessor->/radius.par.val", "source": "/magnitude", "sourceHandle": "out.accessor", "target": "/radius", "targetHandle": "par.val" },
    { "id": "/radius.out.scaled->/points.par.getRadius", "source": "/radius", "sourceHandle": "out.scaled", "target": "/points", "targetHandle": "par.getRadius" }
  ]
}
```

Other expressions that read the row:

```js
d.properties.population / 1000            // a number from a GeoJSON feature
d.delayed ? '#ff4040' : '#40c0ff'          // a color chosen per row
[d.lng, d.lat, d.altitude_m]              // a 3D position
```
